Assessment & Plan:

1. Left-sided hearing loss with facial numbness  
   – Assessment: Suspected Bell’s palsy.  
   – Differential: central nervous system lesion (e.g., stroke, acoustic neuroma), otitis media, recurrent labyrinthitis.  
   – Investigations planned: comprehensive face-to-face neurological exam, otoscopic exam; further tests (e.g., audiogram, imaging) to be considered based on findings.  
   – Treatment planned: to be determined following examination (e.g., corticosteroids if Bell’s palsy confirmed).  
   – Relevant referrals: urgent same-day GP clinic appointment arranged.

2. Health-related anxiety  
   – Assessment: situational anxiety secondary to neurological symptoms.  
   – Treatment planned: reassurance provided; advised that physical examination will give definitive answers; encouraged to attend appointment today.  
   – Follow-up: review anxiety level after diagnostic clarification.
